L0@P0: 1
L1@P0: ANNEX I
L2@P0-1: SUMMARY OF PRODUCT CHARACTERISTICS2
L3@P1: 1. NAME OF THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT
L4@P1: Glivec 100 mg film-coated tablets
L5@P1: Glivec 400 mg film-coated tablets
L6@P1: 2. QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION
L7@P1: Glivec 100 mg film-coated tablets
L8@P1: Each film-coated tablet contains 100 mg imatinib (as mesilate).
L9@P1: Glivec 400 mg film-coated tablets
L10@P1: Each film-coated tablet contains 400 mg imatinib (as mesilate).
L11@P1: For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
L12@P1: 3. PHARMACEUTICAL FORM
L13@P1: Film-coated tablet
L14@P1: Glivec 100 mg film-coated tablets
L15@P1: Very dark yellow to brownish-orange film-coated tablet, round with “NVR” on one side and “SA” and
L16@P1: score on the other side.
L17@P1: Glivec 400 mg film-coated tablets
L18@P1: Very dark yellow to brownish-orange, ovaloid, biconvex film-coated tablet with bevelled edges.
L19@P1: Debossed with “400” on one side and score on the other side with “SL” on each side of the score.
L20@P1: The film-coated tablets can be divided into equal doses.
L21@P1: 4. CLINICAL PARTICULARS
L22@P1: 4.1 Therapeutic indications
L23@P1: Glivec is indicated for the treatment of
L24@P1: • adult and paediatric patients with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome (bcr-abl) positive
L25@P1: (Ph+) chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) for whom bone marrow transplantation is not
L26@P1: considered as the first line of treatment.
L27@P1: • adult and paediatric patients with Ph+ CML in chronic phase after failure of interferon-alpha
L28@P1: therapy, or in accelerated phase or blast crisis.
L29@P1: • adult and paediatric patients with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome positive acute
L30@P1: lymphoblastic leukaemia (Ph+ ALL) integrated with chemotherapy.
L31@P1: • adult patients with relapsed or refractory Ph+ ALL as monotherapy.
L32@P1: • adult patients with myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative diseases (MDS/MPD) associated with
L33@P1: platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) gene re-arrangements.
L34@P1: • adult patients with advanced hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) and/or chronic eosinophilic
L35@P1: leukaemia (CEL) with FIP1L1-PDGFR rearrangement.
L36@P1-2: The effect of Glivec on the outcome of bone marrow transplantation has not been determined.3
L37@P2: Glivec is indicated for
L38@P2: • the treatment of adult patients with Kit (CD 117) positive unresectable and/or metastatic
L39@P2: malignant gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST).
L40@P2: • the adjuvant treatment of adult patients who are at significant risk of relapse following resection
L41@P2: of Kit (CD117)-positive GIST. Patients who have a low or very low risk of recurrence should
L42@P2: not receive adjuvant treatment.
L43@P2: • the treatment of adult patients with unresectable dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) and
L44@P2: adult patients with recurrent and/or metastatic DFSP who are not eligible for surgery.
L45@P2: In adult and paediatric patients, the effectiveness of Glivec is based on overall haematological and
L46@P2: cytogenetic response rates and progression-free survival in CML, on haematological and cytogenetic
L47@P2: response rates in Ph+ ALL, MDS/MPD, on haematological response rates in HES/CEL and on
L48@P2: objective response rates in adult patients with unresectable and/or metastatic GIST and DFSP and on
L49@P2: recurrence-free survival in adjuvant GIST. The experience with Glivec in patients with MDS/MPD
L50@P2: associated with PDGFR gene re-arrangements is very limited (see section 5.1). Except in newly
L51@P2: diagnosed chronic phase CML, there are no controlled trials demonstrating a clinical benefit or
L52@P2: increased survival for these diseases.
L53@P2: 4.2 Posology and method of administration
L54@P2: Therapy should be initiated by a physician experienced in the treatment of patients with
L55@P2: haematological malignancies and malignant sarcomas, as appropriate.
L56@P2: For doses other than 400 mg and 800 mg (see dosage recommendation below), 100 mg and 400 mg
L57@P2: divisible tablets are available.
L58@P2: The prescribed dose should be administered orally with a meal and a large glass of water to minimise
L59@P2: the risk of gastrointestinal irritations. Doses of 400 mg or 600 mg should be administered once daily,
L60@P2: whereas a daily dose of 800 mg should be administered as 400 mg twice a day, in the morning and in
L61@P2: the evening.
L62@P2: For patients unable to swallow the film-coated tablets, the tablets may be dispersed in a glass of still
L63@P2: water or apple juice. The required number of tablets should be placed in the appropriate volume of
L64@P2: beverage (approximately 50 ml for a 100 mg tablet, and 200 ml for a 400 mg tablet) and stirred with a
L65@P2: spoon. The suspension should be administered immediately after complete disintegration of the
L66@P2: tablet(s).
L67@P2: Posology for CML in adult patients
L68@P2: The recommended dosage of Glivec is 400 mg/day for adult patients in chronic phase CML. Chronic
L69@P2: phase CML is defined when all of the following criteria are met: blasts < 15% in blood and bone
L70@P2: marrow, peripheral blood basophils < 20%, platelets > 100 x 109/l.
L71@P2: The recommended dosage of Glivec is 600 mg/day for adult patients in accelerated phase. Accelerated
L72@P2: phase is defined by the presence of any of the following: blasts  15% but < 30% in blood or bone
L73@P2: marrow, blasts plus promyelocytes  30% in blood or bone marrow (providing < 30% blasts),
L74@P2: peripheral blood basophils  20%, platelets < 100 x 109/l unrelated to therapy.
L75@P2: The recommended dose of Glivec is 600 mg/day for adult patients in blast crisis. Blast crisis is defined
L76@P2: as blasts  30% in blood or bone marrow or extramedullary disease other than hepatosplenomegaly.
L77@P2: Treatment duration: In clinical trials, treatment with Glivec was continued until disease progression.
L78@P2: The effect of stopping treatment after the achievement of a complete cytogenetic response has not
L79@P2-3: been investigated.4
L80@P3: Dose increases from 400 mg to 600 mg or 800 mg in patients with chronic phase disease, or from
L81@P3: 600 mg to a maximum of 800 mg (given as 400 mg twice daily) in patients with accelerated phase or
L82@P3: blast crisis may be considered in the absence of severe adverse drug reaction and severe nonleukaemia-related neutropenia or thrombocytopenia in the following circumstances: disease
L83@P3: progression (at any time); failure to achieve a satisfactory haematological response after at least
L84@P3: 3 months of treatment; failure to achieve a cytogenetic response after 12 months of treatment; or loss
L85@P3: of a previously achieved haematological and/or cytogenetic response. Patients should be monitored
L86@P3: closely following dose escalation given the potential for an increased incidence of adverse reactions at
L87@P3: higher dosages.
L88@P3: Posology for CML in children
L89@P3: Dosing for children should be on the basis of body surface area (mg/m2). The dose of 340 mg/m2daily
L90@P3: is recommended for children with chronic phase CML and advanced phase CML (not to exceed the
L91@P3: total dose of 800 mg). Treatment can be given as a once daily dose or alternatively the daily dose may
L92@P3: be split into two administrations – one in the morning and one in the evening. The dose
L93@P3: recommendation is currently based on a small number of paediatric patients (see sections 5.1 and 5.2).
L94@P3: There is no experience with the treatment of children below 2 years of age.
L95@P3: Dose increases from 340 mg/m2daily to 570 mg/m2daily (not to exceed the total dose of 800 mg) may
L96@P3: be considered in children in the absence of severe adverse drug reaction and severe non-leukaemiarelated neutropenia or thrombocytopenia in the following circumstances: disease progression (at any
L97@P3: time); failure to achieve a satisfactory haematological response after at least 3 months of treatment;
L98@P3: failure to achieve a cytogenetic response after 12 months of treatment; or loss of a previously achieved
L99@P3: haematological and/or cytogenetic response. Patients should be monitored closely following dose
L100@P3: escalation given the potential for an increased incidence of adverse reactions at higher dosages.
L101@P3: Posology for Ph+ ALL in adult patients
L102@P3: The recommended dose of Glivec is 600 mg/day for adult patients with Ph+ ALL. Haematological
L103@P3: experts in the management of this disease should supervise the therapy throughout all phases of care.
L104@P3: Treatment schedule: On the basis of the existing data, Glivec has been shown to be effective and safe

L2@P0-1: SUMMARY OF PRODUCT CHARACTERISTICS2
L3@P1: 1. NAME OF THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT
L4@P1: Stivarga 40 mg film-coated tablets.
L5@P1: 2. QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION
L6@P1: Each film-coated tablet contains 40 mg of regorafenib.
L7@P1: Excipients with known effect
L8@P1: Each daily dose of 160 mg contains 2.438 mmol (or 56.06 mg) of sodium (see section 4.4).
L9@P1: Each daily dose of 160 mg contains 1.68 mg of lecithin (derived from soya) (see section 4.4).
L10@P1: For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
L11@P1: 3. PHARMACEUTICAL FORM
L12@P1: Film-coated tablet.
L13@P1: Light pink film-coated tablets, oval shaped with a length of 16 mm and a width of 7 mm marked with
L14@P1: ‘BAYER’ on one side and ‘40’ on the other side.
L15@P1: 4. CLINICAL PARTICULARS
L16@P1: 4.1 Therapeutic indications
L17@P1: Stivarga is indicated as monotherapy for the treatment of adult patients with
L18@P1: - metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC) who have been previously treated with, or are not considered
L19@P1: candidates for, available therapies. These include fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy, an
L20@P1: anti-VEGF therapy and an anti-EGFR therapy (see section 5.1)
L21@P1: - unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST) who progressed on or are
L22@P1: intolerant to prior treatment with imatinib and sunitinib
L23@P1: - hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who have been previously treated with sorafenib.
L24@P1: 4.2 Posology and method of administration
L25@P1: Stivarga should be prescribed by physicians experienced in the administration of anticancer therapy.
L26@P1: Posology
L27@P1: The recommended dose of regorafenib is 160 mg (4 tablets of 40 mg) taken once daily for 3 weeks
L28@P1: followed by 1 week off therapy. This 4-week period is considered a treatment cycle.
L29@P1: If a dose is missed, then it should be taken on the same day as soon as the patient remembers. The
L30@P1: patient should not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose. In case of vomiting
L31@P1: after regorafenib administration, the patient should not take additional tablets.
L32@P1: Treatment should continue as long as benefit is observed or until unacceptable toxicity occurs (see
L33@P1: section 4.4).
L34@P1: Patients with performance status (PS) 2 or higher were excluded from clinical studies. There is limited
L35@P1-2: data in patients with PS ≥2.3
L36@P2: Posology adjustments
L37@P2: Dose interruptions and/or dose reductions may be required based on individual safety and tolerability.
L38@P2: Dose modifications are to be applied in 40 mg (one tablet) steps. The lowest recommended daily dose
L39@P2: is 80 mg. The maximum daily dose is 160 mg.
L40@P2: For recommended dose modifications and measures in case of hand-foot skin reaction
L41@P2: (HFSR)/palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome see Table 1.

L88@P2: For recommended measures and dose modifications in case of worsening of liver function tests
L89@P2-3: considered related to treatment with Stivarga see Table 2 (see also section 4.4).4

L123@P3: to baseline.

L125@P3: develop elevated transaminases should be managed as
L126@P3: per the above outlined recommendations for the
L127@P3: respective observed elevation of ALT and/or AST.
L128@P3: Hepatic impairment
L129@P3: Regorafenib is eliminated mainly via the hepatic route.
L130@P3: In clinical studies, no relevant differences in exposure, safety or efficacy were observed between
L131@P3: patients with mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A) and normal hepatic function. No dose
L132@P3: adjustment is required in patients with mild hepatic impairment. Since only limited data are available
L133@P3: for patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child Pugh B), no dose recommendation can be
L134@P3: provided. Close monitoring of overall safety is recommended in these patients (see sections 4.4
L135@P3: and 5.2).
L136@P3: Stivarga is not recommended for use in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) as
L137@P3: Stivarga has not been studied in this population.
L138@P3: Renal impairment
L139@P3: Available clinical data indicate similar exposure of regorafenib and its metabolites M-2 and M-5 in
L140@P3: patients with mild, moderate or severe renal impairment compared to patients with normal renal
L141@P3: function. No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild, moderate or severe renal impairment
L142@P3: (see also section 5.2).
L143@P3: Elderly population
L144@P3: In clinical studies, no relevant differences in exposure, safety or efficacy were observed between
L145@P3: elderly (aged 65 years and above) and younger patients (see also section 5.2).
L146@P3: Gender
L147@P3: In clinical studies, no relevant differences in exposure, safety or efficacy were observed between male
L148@P3: and female patients. No dose adjustment is necessary based on gender (see also section 5.2).
L149@P3: Ethnic differences
L150@P3: In clinical studies, no relevant differences in exposure or efficacy were observed between patients of
L151@P3: different ethnic groups. A higher incidence of hand foot skin reaction (HFSR)/palmar-plantar
L152@P3-4: erythrodysesthesia syndrome, severe liver function test abnormalities and hepatic dysfunction was 5
L153@P4: observed in Asian (in particular Japanese) patients treated with Stivarga compared with Caucasians.

L0@P0: 1
L1@P0: ANNEX I
L2@P0-1: SUMMARY OF PRODUCT CHARACTERISTICS2
L3@P1: 1. NAME OF THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT
L4@P1: Votrient 200 mg film-coated tablets
L5@P1: Votrient 400 mg film-coated tablets
L6@P1: 2. QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION
L7@P1: Votrient 200 mg film-coated tablets
L8@P1: Each film-coated tablet contains 200 mg pazopanib (as hydrochloride).
L9@P1: Votrient 400 mg film-coated tablets
L10@P1: Each film-coated tablet contains 400 mg pazopanib (as hydrochloride).
L11@P1: For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
L12@P1: 3. PHARMACEUTICAL FORM
L13@P1: Film-coated tablet.
L14@P1: Votrient 200 mg film-coated tablets
L15@P1: Capsule-shaped, pink, film-coated tablet with GS JT debossed on one side.
L16@P1: Votrient 400 mg film-coated tablets
L17@P1: Capsule-shaped, white, film-coated tablet with GS UHL debossed on one side.
L18@P1: 4. CLINICAL PARTICULARS
L19@P1: 4.1 Therapeutic indications
L20@P1: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC)
L21@P1: Votrient is indicated in adults for the first-line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and
L22@P1: for patients who have received prior cytokine therapy for advanced disease.
L23@P1: Soft-tissue sarcoma (STS)
L24@P1: Votrient is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with selective subtypes of advanced soft-tissue
L25@P1: sarcoma (STS) who have received prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease or who have progressed
L26@P1: within 12 months after (neo) adjuvant therapy.
L27@P1: Efficacy and safety has only been established in certain STS histological tumour subtypes (see
L28@P1: section 5.1).
L29@P1: 4.2 Posology and method of administration
L30@P1: Votrient treatment should only be initiated by a physician experienced in the administration of
L31@P1-2: anti-cancer medicinal products.3
L32@P2: Posology
L33@P2: Adults
L34@P2: The recommended dose of pazopanib for the treatment of RCC or STS is 800 mg once daily.
L35@P2: Dose modifications
L36@P2: Dose modification (decrease or increase) should be in 200 mg decrements or increments in a stepwise
L37@P2: fashion based on individual tolerability in order to manage adverse reactions. The dose of pazopanib
L38@P2: should not exceed 800 mg.
L39@P2: Paediatric population
L40@P2: Pazopanib should not be used in children younger than 2 years of age because of safety concerns with
L41@P2: regard to organ growth and maturation (see sections 4.4 and 5.3).
L42@P2: The safety and efficacy of pazopanib in children aged 2 to 18 years of age have not yet been
L43@P2: established.
L44@P2: Currently available data are described in sections 4.8, 5.1 and 5.2 but no recommendation on a posology
L45@P2: can be made.
L46@P2: Elderly
L47@P2: There are limited data on the use of pazopanib in patients aged 65 years and older. In the RCC studies
L48@P2: of pazopanib, overall no clinically significant differences in safety of pazopanib were observed
L49@P2: between subjects aged at least 65 years and younger subjects. Clinical experience has not identified
L50@P2: differences in responses between the elderly and younger patients, but greater sensitivity of some
L51@P2: elderly patients cannot be ruled out.
L52@P2: Renal impairment
L53@P2: Renal impairment is unlikely to have a clinically relevant effect on pazopanib pharmacokinetics given
L54@P2: the low renal excretion of pazopanib and metabolites (see section 5.2). Therefore, no dose adjustment
L55@P2: is required in patients with creatinine clearance above 30 ml/min. Caution is advised in patients with
L56@P2: creatinine clearance below 30 ml/min as there is no experience of pazopanib in this patient population.
L57@P2: Hepatic impairment
L58@P2: Dosing recommendations in hepatically impaired patients are based on pharmacokinetic studies of
L59@P2: pazopanib in patients with varying degrees of hepatic dysfunction (see section 5.2). All patients should
L60@P2: have liver function tests to determine whether they have hepatic impairment before starting and during
L61@P2: pazopanib therapy (see section 4.4). Administration of pazopanib to patients with mild or moderate
L62@P2: hepatic impairment should be undertaken with caution and close monitoring of tolerability. 800 mg
L63@P2: pazopanib once daily is the recommended dose in patients with mild abnormalities in serum liver tests
L64@P2: (defined either as normal bilirubin and any degree of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation or as
L65@P2: an elevation of bilirubin (>35% direct) up to 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) regardless of the ALT
L66@P2: value). A reduced pazopanib dose of 200 mg once daily is recommended in patients with moderate
L67@P2: hepatic impairment (defined as an elevation of bilirubin >1.5 to 3 x ULN regardless of the ALT value)
L68@P2: (see section 5.2).
L69@P2: Pazopanib is not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment (defined as total bilirubin
L70@P2: >3 x ULN regardless of the ALT value).
L71@P2: See section 4.4 for liver monitoring and dose modification for patients with drug-induced
L72@P2: hepatotoxicity.
L73@P2: Method of administration
L74@P2: Pazopanib is for oral use. It should be taken without food, at least one hour before or two hours after a
L75@P2: meal (see section 5.2). The film-coated tablets should be taken whole with water and not broken or
L76@P2-3: crushed (see section 5.2).4
L77@P3: 4.3 Contraindications
L78@P3: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
L79@P3: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use
L80@P3: Hepatic effects
L81@P3: Cases of hepatic failure (including fatalities) have been reported during use of pazopanib.
L82@P3: Administration of pazopanib to patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment should be
L83@P3: undertaken with caution and close monitoring. 800 mg pazopanib once daily is the recommended dose
L84@P3: in patients with mild abnormalities in serum liver tests (either normal bilirubin and any degree of ALT
L85@P3: elevation or elevation of bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN regardless of the ALT value). A reduced pazopanib
L86@P3: dose of 200 mg once daily is recommended in patients with moderate hepatic impairment (elevation of
L87@P3: bilirubin >1.5 to 3 x ULN regardless of the ALT value) (see sections 4.2 and 5.2). Pazopanib is not
L88@P3: recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin >3 x ULN regardless of the
L89@P3: ALT value) (see sections 4.2 and 5.2). Exposure at a 200 mg dose is markedly reduced, though highly
L90@P3: variable, in these patients, with values considered insufficient to obtain a clinically relevant effect.
L91@P3: In clinical studies with pazopanib, increase in serum transaminases (ALT, aspartate aminotransferase
L92@P3: [AST]) and bilirubin were observed (see section 4.8). In the majority of the cases, isolated increases in
L93@P3: ALT and AST have been reported, without concomitant elevations of alkaline phosphatase or
L94@P3: bilirubin. Patients over 60 years of age may be at greater risk for mild (>3 x ULN) to severe
L95@P3: (>8 x ULN) elevation of ALT. Patients who carry the HLA-B*57:01 allele have an increased risk of
L96@P3: pazopanib-associated ALT elevations. Liver function should be monitored in all subjects receiving
